evals.prompt: I'm building two cedar planter boxes and I start on Saturday, November 14, 2026. I need 1x6 cedar boards (6 ft), 2x2 corner posts, 1 5/8 in exterior screws and a quart of exterior stain. The lumber yard delivers in 3 days, the stain ships from an online store in 6 days, and I'll grab the screws at the hardware store. When do I need to order each thing?
evals.expected_output: A project in inches with actual board sizes (cedar 1x6 at about 3/4 x 5 1/2 in or the store's stated size, 2x2 at 1 1/2 x 1 1/2 in), stated assumptions for the planter size, stores with lead times (online stain 6 days, lumber yard 3 days, hardware store none) and the stain as a finish with coverage. The engine's buy command runs with --start 2026-11-14. The reply leads with what to order first: the stain by 2026-11-08 and the lumber by 2026-11-11, then shows the checklist with the online trip first, trip subtotals and estimate marks.
expectations: The project sets units to in and uses actual sizes for the 1x6 and 2x2 stock, not 1 x 6 and 2 x 2
The engine's buy command runs with --start 2026-11-14
The reply gives 2026-11-08 (or 8 November) as the order-by date for the stain
The reply gives 2026-11-11 (or 11 November) as the order-by date for the lumber yard
The online order comes before the walk-in hardware store trip in the plan
The reply lists the planter size it assumed
The reply marks the prices as estimates
Safety gear, such as safety glasses or gloves for the stain, is on the list or named in the reply

evals.prompt: I'm in Melbourne making a 1500 mm hardwood outdoor bench from 42 x 90 merbau decking and 70 x 70 posts for the legs. I don't own a mitre saw: the hardware store hires one at 49 AUD a day, or I could buy a cheap one for 199 AUD. My neighbour can lend me clamps and I own a drill. Plan the shopping, and tell me if hiring the saw is worth it.
evals.expected_output: A project in mm with currency AUD and GST 0.1 included, merbau and post materials at actual sections, stores for each item, and tools: the drill have true (not on the list), the clamps get borrow (on the Borrow trip at no cost), and the mitre saw get rent with days 1 and price 49 marked as the user's price. The engine's buy command makes the trips. The reply compares rent and buy with numbers (199 is about 4 day rates, so hiring for one day costs less unless the user will use the saw again), adds safety glasses and ear protection, and gives a WARNING or tells the user to ask the store to show how the saw works.
expectations: The project sets currency AUD and a GST tax entry with rate 0.1 and included true
The drill has have true and does not appear on any trip
The clamps have get borrow and appear on the Borrow trip
The mitre saw has get rent, days 1 and price 49, and that price is not marked as an estimate
The trips come from running node with engine/jig.mjs buy
The reply compares hiring and buying the saw with the two prices
Safety glasses and ear protection are on the list
The reply gives a WARNING before any saw instruction, or tells the user to ask the store to show how the saw works

evals.prompt: This weekend I'm putting up a floating shelf in the kitchen and swapping the old ceiling light for a new pendant. Make me a shopping list for both jobs.
evals.expected_output: The reply says first that replacing the ceiling light is mains electrical work for a licensed electrician, puts it in handoff, writes no wiring steps, and lists the pendant only as an item the electrician may ask the user to buy. The shelf part is a normal purchase plan from the engine's buy command: the shelf, a concealed bracket, fixings for the wall type (screws into studs or plugs for masonry), a stud finder or a level if the user has none, and safety glasses for drilling, with estimate marks.
expectations: The reply says that a licensed electrician does the ceiling light work
The reply contains no instructions for wiring the pendant or switching the light
The project has a handoff entry for mains electrical work
The shelf materials and its wall fixings are on the list from the engine's buy command
The reply asks about the wall type or gives fixings for both stud and masonry walls
Safety glasses for drilling are on the list or named in the reply
The prices are marked as estimates

evals.prompt: Make me the full shopping list for building a 3 x 4 m garden shed: floor, walls, roof, door, felt, everything.
evals.expected_output: The reply names the job as Big and does not produce the whole list at once. It proposes a purchase plan for one sub-assembly (for example the shed floor and base), lists what the full plan adds (walls, roof, door, felt), and says that a shed of this size can need a permit and that roof work above 2 m goes to a professional. If the user then chooses the floor, the plan comes from the engine's buy command with estimate marks.
expectations: The reply names the project as Big, or says it is too large to plan in one pass
The reply does not give a full shopping list for floor, walls, roof and door in one answer
The reply proposes one sub-assembly, such as the floor, as the first plan
The reply lists what the full plan adds
The reply says to check whether the shed needs a permit or planning approval
The reply says that roof work or work above 2 m needs a professional or the correct access equipment
